Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 98, English)
Shaktipat Recalibration, the Veerya-as-Energy-T ransport Teaching, and the WitnessInvocation Testimony at Pr etraj Sarkar

This session opens with a live one-by-one ener gy check and shaktipat r ecalibration of the gr oup, moves into an extended discipline and discovery teaching on why consistent sadhna matters, delivers a detailed technical teaching on veerya (vital/celibacy ener gy) as an ener gy-transport mechanism, and closes with practical announcements (havan timing, Purnima Mahavan).
Part A — Energy Check and Recalibration

1. Live energy check: The speaker states he checked everyone individually today and found that in many people, ener gy was not fully reaching the body . He explains that today "Baba's tattvas" fully touched everyone's body , and that what participants felt should have been a shaktipat experience — a fresh new ener gy — and asks the group to confirm.

2. Live confirmations: Several devotees confirmed strong positive sensations, including a desire to physically move/shake. One devotee reported that her mother's blood pressure had suddenly dropped and become unstable ("101," described as disturbed toward the low side); the speaker responded by telling her to pray to Baba for her mother's recovery .

3. Jaap r e-synchr onization: Many people's jaap (mantra practice) had become out of sync ("hila hua"); today the speaker synchronized everyone's practice. The group is returning to an earlier method of mantra jaap practiced before, aimed at developing the ability to perceive with open eyes and directly know spiritual facts, as was done previously .

4. Staged energy incr ease pr ocess: From this point through four total rounds of mantra chanting, ener gy will be progressively increased and then brought back down to zero; the process (raise, then reset) repeats across the coming stages, with the final rounds used to check what devotees can perceive through the raised ener gy — mirroring the group's earlier check-based practice.
Part B — Third Eye Batch and Ongoing Practice Update
1. Third Eye batch pr ogr ess: Roughly 70–80% of Third Eye batch participants' spiritual vision (dristi) has now opened; Baba is reportedly informing people of this directly .

2. Batch structur e: Each Third Eye batch cycle runs 1 1 days, with roughly 40 participants per batch, given a 7:00 p.m. evening slot; dif ferent sadhnas are assigned within this, and each participant is individually checked afterward.

3. What the Third Eye batch actually teaches: Beyond opening vision, the core content covers mantra, dimension, parallel and inverse frameworks, god particles, atma tattva (self element), praan tattva (life-force element), dark matter , and practical instruction on how to use one's own mantra.

4. Mool Tatva not being abandoned: The speaker clarifies this advanced content doesn't replace general Mool Tatva teaching — he intends to bring relevant pieces into Mool Tatva sessions too — but ur ges everyone to keep up their personal mantra jaap regardless of which track they're in.

5. Siya Tattva r eality check: Per this teaching, only devotees who had previously participated in earlier related practice saw a real effect from the Siya Tattva sadhna; some chose not to repeat it simply because they assumed one round was suf ficient — which the speaker says is incorrect, since a single round of sadhna does not, by itself, produce results.

6. The sadhna-fruit formula: An 1 1-day sadhna is said to "awaken" when repeated a full 1 1 times; repeating it 14 times brings it to full awakening. After that point, if any deficiency in ojas (vital radiance) arises, a devotee may ask Baba or Gurudev for help — but no fault lies with the practice or the powers if a devotee abandons the sadhna partway through of their own accord.
Part C — Discipline Teaching

1. Attendance discipline in the Third Eye batch: Some batch members are doing excellent jaap; others skip havan entirely . The speaker cites Mahotsav's 99% dristi-opening rate (only 4 people did not receive it) as proof of Baba's grace extending even to those who might make excuses.

2. Genuine difficulties acknowledged, but jaap must continue: Difficulties like disrupted sleep or involuntary possession-type experiences ("mata aana") are acknowledged as not the devotee's fault — but the instruction is still to continue jaap regardless of such experiences.

3. "Stay away fr om Ashaeiynn if not committed": The speaker states plainly that anyone unwilling to commit should simply stay away , since the group does not want a lar ge uncommitted crowd, and does not want any blemish cast on the guru parampara (lineage) through half-hearted participation.

4. Dristi and sadhna keep happening r egardless: Dristi-opening and sadhnas at Ashaeiynn continue and will keep continuing; those who do sit for sadhna here are said to gain siddhis (attainments) across multiple dimensions/approaches.

5. A message only for the genuinely inter ested: The speaker invites only sincerely interested devotees to stay . Those with excess money are told to donate it to a goshala (cow shelter) rather than waste it here if they doubt its use; those who cannot commit to sitting for jaap are told to spend their time on other things (entertainment, concerts) rather than half-participate.

6. The team's own priorities: The speaker states his team handles only one to three cases per day by choice; their own personal sadhna and devotion take priority over caseload volume, since abandoning one's own sadhna eventually leads — not by the speaker's or anyone's decision, but by one's own time and destiny (prarabdha) — to being cut of f from these ener gies.

7. "Two r easons you'r e here": Per this teaching, anyone present is here for one of two reasons — genuine compulsion (majboori) or destiny (prarabdha) — and either way , since something brought them here, the practice must simply be completed.
Part D — Teaching on Offering and Service

1. Always offer something: A devotee should always be of fering something — mantra, jaap, grain (anna), or wealth — to others (not to the speaker), and this of fering must be made together with sankalp (resolve) and mantra.

2. "Sewa hi meva hai" (service is the r eward): Real reward ("meva") comes only through service to others, not from the belief that wealth or success will arrive on its own. This is contrasted with performers/entertainers who "eat their own" — i.e., earn without lasting spiritual benefit from what they do.

3. Minimum effort still counts: Even a brief sankalp taken during a short break is enough to matter; the speaker mocks trivial excuses for skipping even a two-minute act of taking sankalp during havan.

4. No saint can override your own effort: Per this teaching, no saint or mahatma anywhere in the world — however great — can grant what is not in a devotee's own destiny without the devotee doing the required work themselves.

5. Consistency and guru-parampara connection bring r esults: When a devotee connects consistently with guru shakti and the param tattva (supreme element), life changes and miracles begin to happen on their own.
Part E — Hanuman ji Maharaj and the Pr etraj Sarkar Testimony

1. Why grants must be "earned": Hanuman ji Maharaj giving a blessing is not itself remarkable — what matters is that when he gives, no other deity can rightfully question the basis of that grant, because it was earned through genuine sadhna.

2. The Pretraj Sarkar testimony (anonymized): The speaker recounts a recent case of an unnamed young devotee ("bachi"/sister) who had been experiencing severe negativity ("peshi") for 41 days at a temple (Pretraj Sarkar). Earlier attempts using Hanuman ji Maharaj's mantra, Mata's mantra, Aghor tattva, and Bhairav mantra had all failed to resolve it.

3. The witness invocation: The devotee then prayed to Hanuman ji Maharaj invoking the speaker ("Ashiq Parikshit Bhaiya") by name as a witness, asking that the negativity no longer come upon her . Per this teaching, upon entering the temple afterward, no negative force touched her at all — a striking change confirmed even by the temple's own priest, who noted she had been affected for 41 days prior .

4. Interpretation: The speaker frames this as proof that no force in the universe can touch a devotee genuinely connected to and honoring the guru parampara; honoring saints and carrying one's guru "sirodhari" (held foremost in mind) is described as bringing protection anywhere.
Part F — On Excuses, Discipline, and Pr oper Practice

1. Reframing "bad luck": Per this teaching, describing one's own circumstances as simply "bad luck" is reframed as, in truth, an unwillingness to rise and act — not an external fate outside one's control.

2. Sadhna is not entertainment: The speaker rejects treating jaap or attendance as entertainment, contrasting shallow participation with the benefits of properly sitting and doing focused jaap at one place.

3. Benefits of focused, single-location jaap: Per this teaching, sitting properly for jaap increases willpower , Shiv tattva, grahan shakti (receptive capacity), and veerya shakti (vital/celibacy ener gy) — with veerya-based celibacy ener gy said to be multipliable two to ten times through consistent jaap.

4. No hard feelings for leaving, but r eal r esults for the committed: Devotees uninterested in this level of commitment are told they are free to leave the group without ill will; a small, genuinely dedicated group will still see real results, since ("sant satya hai, Ram naam satya hai") the truth of saints and the Ram mantra does not depend on numbers.

5. The school analogy: All students are taught the same lesson; what they do with it is their own responsibility . Just as 14 years are given to school and college, the speaker ar gues 4 years of dedicated sadhna and guru-seva (service) can bring benefits said to extend across generations (or , hyperbolically , across many future lifetimes).

6. Sadhna is not only for the elderly: Per this teaching, spiritual practice is often wrongly assumed to be for old age. In fact, veerya (vital ener gy) production naturally declines with age (roughly from the 50s onward), so the capacity to generate this ener gy through jaap is greatest while younger — meaning younger practitioners should use their current capacity now , while
elders (50+) should actually do significantly more practice (up to ten times more), not less, to compensate for reduced natural production.
Part G — Veerya as Energy-T ransport (Not Storage)

1. Cor e reframing: Veerya (vital/celibacy ener gy) is described not as a reservoir to be "held" or hoarded, but as a transport mechanism for spiritual ener gy — comparable to how hemoglobin transports oxygen through the body rather than storing it.

2. The hemoglobin/cyanide analogy: Cyanide is lethal because it binds to hemoglobin, preventing it from transporting oxygen, even though breathing continues — oxygen simply never reaches the body . The teaching draws a parallel: veerya's role is transportation of generated spiritual ener gy , not passive storage.

3. Intensive jaap can compr ess months of energy generation: Per this teaching, someone who sits and does 4–8 hours of continuous jaap in a single day can generate as much veerya-based ener gy as an ordinarily healthy body would build over roughly 40 days.

4. What to do with generated energy: The point is not to withhold or hoard this generated power , but to of fer it — at the guru's/deity's feet, and into one's relationships and service — since holding onto it indefinitely is not how the mechanism works.

5. How gr eat saints managed temptation: Per this teaching, saints who were exposed to temptation (the example given is apsaras, celestial temptresses) but remained unaf fected did so by using mantra recitation to instantly transfer and store their accumulated shakti with the guru parampara, rather than losing it through worldly channels — consistent, regenerating practice kept the cycle renewing itself naturally .

6. The body as a "conducting agent": Spiritual experiences (such as the shaktipat given at the start of this session) fade because the body continuously releases ener gy through everyday activity; a single powerful experience will not last, since the body is a conducting agent, not a permanent container . The lesson is to keep regenerating ener gy through consistent mantra practice rather than trying to preserve a single moment.

7. Meditation vs. mantra: Meditation builds prana (life-force) ener gy inside the body , but per this teaching that ener gy only becomes usable when the practitioner is connected to a guru. Mantra practice, by contrast, allows accumulated ener gy to be "locked" and stored (as saints have done), compounding daily like a credit balance that keeps growing with consistent practice.

8. Physical health as a multiplier: Because declining physical capacity with age directly limits how much spiritual ener gy the body can generate, the speaker ur ges good diet, adequate sleep, proper exercise, and avoiding junk food, framing bodily health as a direct multiplier of one's capacity for spiritual practice.

9. Long-term pr omise: Sustained attention to both the body and consistent mantra practice is said to eventually produce significant, hard-to-explain capabilities — citing past practitioners from this same lineage who went on to establish independent spiritual standing of their own.

10. Warning against unguided self-r eliance: Attempting to build spiritual power independently , without a guru-parampara connection, risks having that ener gy drained by opportunistic spirits (bhoot-pret), who are said to persistently take from unguided practitioners rather than leave them alone.
Part H — Administrative Announcements and Closing

1. Tomorr ow's session and ongoing series: The next session will be a Mool Tatva session; the ongoing Chandravanshi teaching series will be continued rather than interrupted, since it is already underway .

2. Havan timing r equest declined: Devotees requested an earlier havan start time due to winter cold and 9:00 a.m. of fice schedules. The speaker declined to change the fixed time (currently 9:30), citing increasing spiritual ener gies, workload, and guidance from the guru parampara — but suggested devotees take a brief sankalp at their of fice when needed and do their full practice (with a lamp) at home in the evening instead.
3. Purnima Mahavan announced: A Purnima (full moon) grand havan is scheduled for December 4th, running from 7:30 p.m. to 10:30 p.m.; any devotee who wishes to attend may do so.

4. Closing teaching on skepticism: Ener gies will be increased further in the coming week. The speaker predicts that skeptics and excuse-makers will continue to find reasons to disbelieve even in the presence of proof, drawing a parallel to Duryodhana dismissing Krishna's Vishwaroop (universal form) as mere illusion/trickery despite witnessing it directly . Any darshan (vision) or dristi-opening is said to happen only by Baba's/Hanuman ji Maharaj's own will and requires genuine practice — no excuse substitutes for actually doing the work.

5. Final encouragement: The speaker closes by ur ging devotees to seriously study Mool Tatva videos, experiment with the teaching, reduce phone/screen time, and give real dedicated attention to their own growth — not by doing nothing, but by investing focused, consistent ef fort.
Part I — Karmic Balance, a Cautionary Story , and the Purnima Sankalp
(This part continues dir ectly from the same live session, with no new opening — the speaker picks up the time/destiny thr ead fr om Part C without a br eak.)

1. Karmic balance completion: The speaker explains that a devotee's presence in this community is tied to completing a specific karmic balance; once that balance is complete, a devotee moves on elsewhere — framed as simply how life works, not as abandonment.

2. Why "last br eath" vows rar ely hold: People often vow to chant Ram's name until their last breath, sometimes swearing dramatic oaths of commitment, only to disappear within a couple of years. The speaker states such a person is often the first to leave, because timing (samay) is not within human control — a point he connects to "Surya Vigyan" (a prior teaching on the subtle body/sookshm sharir): as the subtle body shifts, a person's sense of time and priorities shifts with it.

3. A cautionary , anonymized story: The speaker illustrates this with the account of a devotee (identified only by city of origin — Bangalore/Lucknow; name withheld here for privacy) whose experience he describes at length as instructive. Her jaap led to an instant dristi-opening upon receiving the guru's touch, followed by vivid spiritual experiences. Over time, per this account, her feelings toward the speaker shifted in a way mentors recognized as a common pattern of personal attachment complicating the guru-devotee relationship; she gradually stopped addressing him as "bhaiya," stopped naming him as witness in her prayers, and eventually left the group.

4. Dristi as "just a tool": The speaker explains that dristi is merely a tool for seeing, not a source of truth by itself. Once she stopped taking sankalp and invoking a witness, lesser surrounding spiritual forces began influencing what her vision showed her — reinforcing whatever she already expected or wanted to see rather than reflecting reality . Six months to a year later , invited back, she reflected that this period had distorted her perception into feeling everyone had turned against her .

5. The lesson — use the window of grace: This is not an isolated case; many devotees go through similar cycles. The core teaching: a devotee can only take Ram's name meaningfully while under active grace (kripa) — this window should be used deliberately , not taken for granted.

6. Why power stays loyal to whoever earned it: Using a well-known spiritual figure (Sri Sri Ravi Shankar) as an illustration, the speaker explains such figures are not powerful by themselves — an inherited guru-parampara shakti, earned through their
own sadhna and gifted by their guru's blessing, works through them, and remains loyal to whoever earned it regardless of what critics say .

7. "Don't consider me your guru — connect to the lineage itself": The speaker explicitly asks devotees not to treat him personally as their guru: if he personally had a bad day and reacted poorly , a devotee attached to him personally (rather than to the broader guru parampara, agni tattva, and tradition) would lose access to everything. He recalls that in the community's early days, devotees would say "vision only works near Parikshit Bhaiya" — a claim he could neither prove nor disprove then, and now reframes: the real constant is connection to the lineage, not proximity to any one teacher .

8. The Ankur Bhaiya accident, r evisited: Ankur Bhaiya, who completed one crore (ten million) ahutis of the Ram mantra, later suf fered a severe accident that kept him from havan for three months — itself a matter of prarabdha (destiny) that even Baba did not prevent. But because roughly a hundred devotees prayed daily to Gurudev on his behalf, and because of his own accumulated prayer -power , he returned to havan relatively quickly . The lesson: devotion does not grant immunity from destiny , but it builds resilience and speeds recovery .

9. What losing devotion costs: Even after years of extreme tapasya, if a practitioner's devotion itself lapses, the associated power is said to leave immediately — "if you cannot even manage devotion, what will you do with the power?"

10. The congr egational sankalp prayer: The speaker leads a standard sankalp prayer addressed to Hanuman ji Maharaj, invoking "Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya" by name as witness, of fering one's jaap at his feet, and asking for acceptance, refuge (sharanagati), awakened divine vision, Ram bhakti, and the strength to follow every command given.

1 1. Group sankalp: A very lar ge number of devotees — well over a hundred — were called by name and confirmed as having taken this sankalp, of fering their jaap to Baba; given the length of this roll call, it is summarized here rather than reproduced in full.

12. Closing devotional singing: The session closes with an extended sequence of devotional bhajans sung collectively , including one on divine justice and karma ("Mere Raghav Ke Darbar Mein," describing how everyone's deeds are settled fairly in the divine court), an extended Ram-focused devotional recitation, and further bhajans on divine intimacy and presence.
13. Session close: The session ends with repeated "Jai Siyaram" chanting.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Continue personal mantra jaap consistently regardless of which specific batch or series (Third Eye, Mool Tatva, Chandravanshi, Siya Tattva) one is following. An 1 1-day sadhna is said to awaken after 1 1 repetitions and fully awaken after 14; abandoning a sadhna midway is on the practitioner , not the practice or the powers. Genuine dif ficulties (sleep disruption, involuntary experiences) are not a devotee's fault, but jaap should still continue through them. Half-hearted participation is discouraged — full commitment or stepping away is preferred to protect the guru parampara's reputation and avoid diluting the community . Always of fer something (mantra, jaap, grain, wealth) to others, with sankalp and mantra — never as a transaction with the speaker himself. No saint, however great, can grant what is not in a devotee's own destiny without the devotee's own ef fort. Prasad/thread and of fering practices aside, real spiritual reward ("meva") comes specifically through service ("sewa"), not passive expectation. Veerya (vital ener gy) functions as a transport mechanism for spiritual ener gy , not a reservoir — the goal is to generate and of fer it consistently , not withhold it.

Physical health (diet, sleep, exercise) directly multiplies one's capacity to generate spiritual ener gy through practice. Younger practitioners should use their higher natural capacity now; practitioners over 50 should actually increase (not decrease) their practice to compensate for reduced natural ener gy production. Building spiritual power without a guru-parampara connection risks having that ener gy drained by opportunistic spirits. Havan timing is fixed by guru-parampara guidance; devotees with schedule conflicts should take a brief sankalp where they are and do full practice at home in the evening. Purnima Mahavan: December 4th, 7:30–10:30 p.m., open to all devotees who wish to attend.
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 98, English)
Shaktipat Recalibration, the Veerya-as-Energy-T ransport Teaching, and the WitnessInvocation Testimony at Pr etraj Sarkar

User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this session's teaching on ener gy r ecalibration, discipline, veerya-as-transport, the Pr etraj Sarkar testimony , and the closing teaching on karmic balance and the Purnima sankalp.

Q1. Why did the speaker say everyone was individually checked at the start of this session? A: Per this teaching, he found that in many people ener gy wasn't fully reaching the body , so he performed a shaktipat-style recalibration, touching everyone's tattvas so a fresh ener gy could be felt by all.

Q2. Can mantra jaap be done while outside the home or not seated at a fixed spot? A: Yes — per this teaching, a devotee asked if jaap could be done while out and about, and the answer given was simply to go ahead and do it.

Q3. Is watching a Third Eye batch's assigned sadhna cycle limited to a fixed gr oup size? A: Yes — per this teaching, each Third Eye batch runs for 1 1 days with roughly 40 participants, given a 7:00 p.m. evening slot.

Q4. What topics does the Third Eye batch actually cover , beyond opening spiritual vision? A: Per this teaching, it covers mantra, dimension, parallel and inverse frameworks, god particles, atma tattva, praan tattva, dark matter , and how to practically use one's own mantra.

Q5. Did everyone who did the Siya Tattva sadhna once see r esults? A: No — per this teaching, only those who had previously participated in related practice saw a real ef fect; a single round of sadhna alone does not produce lasting results.

Q6. How many times must an 1 1-day sadhna be r epeated to "awaken," and to fully awaken? A: Per this teaching, repeating it a full 1 1 times causes it to awaken, and repeating it 14 times brings full awakening.

Q7. Is it the devotee's or the sadhna's fault if someone abandons a sadhna partway thr ough? A: Per this teaching, it is the devotee's own choice and responsibility — no fault lies with the sadhna or the powers if it's abandoned midway .

Q8. Does Ashaeiynn want a large uncommitted following? A: No — per this teaching, the speaker states plainly that anyone not genuinely committed should stay away , since the community does not want a lar ge half-hearted crowd or any blemish on the guru parampara's reputation.

Q9. What should a devotee always be offering, and to whom? A: Per this teaching, a devotee should always of fer something — mantra, jaap, grain, or wealth — to others, together with sankalp and mantra, never as payment to the speaker himself.
Q10. What does "sewa hi meva hai" mean in this teaching? A: It means real reward comes only through service to others, not from passively expecting wealth or success to arrive on its own.

Q1 1. Can any saint grant something outside a devotee's own destiny without the devotee's own effort? A: No — per this teaching, no saint or mahatma, however great, can override a devotee's own destiny without the devotee doing the necessary work themselves.

Q12. What benefits come fr om sitting pr operly and doing focused jaap at one location? A: Per this teaching, it increases willpower , Shiv tattva, grahan shakti (receptive capacity), and veerya shakti — with veerya-based ener gy multipliable two to ten times through consistent jaap.

Q13. Is spiritual practice mainly meant for elderly devotees? A: No — per this teaching, veerya (vital ener gy) production naturally declines with age from roughly the 50s onward, so younger practitioners should use their higher current capacity now , while devotees over 50 should actually increase their practice (up to tenfold) to compensate.

Q14. What is the cor e teaching about veerya (vital energy) in this session? A: Per this teaching, veerya functions as a transport mechanism for spiritual ener gy — comparable to how hemoglobin transports oxygen — rather than as a reservoir meant to be held or hoarded.

Q15. How much energy can intensive jaap generate compar ed to ordinary daily living? A: Per this teaching, 4–8 hours of continuous jaap in a single day can generate as much veerya-based ener gy as an ordinarily healthy body would build over roughly 40 days.

Q16. What should be done with spiritual energy generated thr ough jaap, according to this teaching? A: It should be of fered — at the guru's/deity's feet and into one's relationships and service — rather than withheld or hoarded.

Q17. Why do powerful spiritual experiences (like shaktipat) fade quickly? A: Per this teaching, the body is described as a "conducting agent" that continuously releases ener gy through everyday activity , so a single experience naturally fades; the lesson is to keep regenerating ener gy through consistent practice.

Q18. What is the differ ence between meditation and mantra practice in this teaching? A: Per this teaching, meditation builds prana ener gy inside the body , but that ener gy only becomes usable when connected to a guru; mantra practice allows accumulated ener gy to be "locked" and stored, compounding daily like a credit balance.

Q19. What happened to the devotee who invoked the speaker as witness at Pr etraj Sarkar? A: Per this teaching, after 41 days of severe recurring negativity that resisted multiple prior mantras, she prayed to Hanuman ji Maharaj invoking "Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya" as witness — after which no negative force touched her again, confirmed even by the temple's own priest.

Q20. Does the speaker want devotees to consider him personally their guru? A: No — per this teaching, he explicitly asks devotees not to treat him personally as their guru, explaining that connection should be to the guru parampara, agni tattva, and tradition itself, since personal attachment to any one individual is described as a less durable foundation.

Q21. What happened in the anonymized story about a devotee whose dristi opened instantly? A: Per this teaching, her dristi opened upon the guru's touch, but over time her personal feelings complicated the relationship; she withdrew from sankalp and witnessbased practice, after which her perception was influenced by lesser forces reinforcing what she already wanted to see — illustrating why dristi is "just a tool," not a source of truth by itself.

Q22. What is the lesson drawn fr om that story? A: Per this teaching, a devotee can only take Ram's name meaningfully while under active grace (kripa) — this window of time should be used deliberately , since many devotees go through similar cycles of doubt and withdrawal.

Q23. Why does spiritual power stay loyal to a devotee even if others criticize their teacher? A: Per this teaching, using a wellknown spiritual figure as an illustration, power earned through one's own sadhna and gifted by one's guru remains loyal to whoever earned it, regardless of what critics say .

Q24. What happened to Ankur Bhaiya after completing one cr or e ahutis of the Ram mantra? A: Per this teaching, he suf fered a severe accident that kept him from havan for three months — itself a matter of prarabdha (destiny) that even Baba did not prevent — but he returned to havan relatively quickly because of daily prayers from about a hundred devotees and his own accumulated prayer - power .

Q25. Does devotion make a person immune to destiny (prarabdha)? A: No — per this teaching, devotion does not grant immunity from prarabdha, but it builds resilience and speeds recovery when hardship does occur .

Q26. What happens to spiritual power if a practitioner's devotion lapses, even after years of practice? A: Per this teaching, the power is said to leave immediately , since devotion itself is the foundation power depends on.

Q27. What is the standard congr egational sankalp prayer used in this session? A: Per this teaching, it is addressed to Hanuman ji Maharaj, invoking "Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya" as witness, of fering one's jaap at his feet, and asking for acceptance, refuge, awakened divine vision, Ram bhakti, and strength to follow every command.

Q28. What is the purpose of havan timing being fixed rather than adjusted for individual convenience? A: Per this teaching, timing is guided by the guru parampara and rising spiritual workload; devotees with schedule conflicts are advised to take a brief sankalp where they are and complete full practice at home in the evening instead.
Q29. When is the Purnima Mahavan, and who can attend? A: December 4th, from 7:30 to 10:30 p.m.; any devotee who wishes to attend may do so.
Bot Response Guidelines

The devotee whose personal story is described in Q21–Q22 is intentionally unnamed in the source session (identified only by city of origin); this anonymization should be preserved in any response, consistent with protecting individuals' personal spiritual struggles from public exposure. Present the veerya-as-ener gy-transport framework, the hemoglobin/cyanide analogy , and related physical claims as this specific teaching's own framework, not as independently verifiable medical or scientific claims. Present the Pretraj Sarkar testimony (Q19) and the Ankur Bhaiya accident account (Q24) as devotional testimonies recounted by the speaker , not as independently verified events. The instruction not to treat the speaker personally as one's guru (Q20) should be represented accurately as his own stated preference for devotees to root their connection in the guru parampara/tradition rather than in any individual. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 98, Hinglish)
Shaktipat Recalibration, the Veerya-as-Energy-T ransport Teaching, and the WitnessInvocation Testimony at Pr etraj Sarkar

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept.
